private.name: Cobod
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series A)

data.narrative:
Material Evolution, a Series A-stage housing and construction company founded by Liz Gilligan and Sam Clark, is evaluated against a limited comp universe of two private peers (Inversion Space and Cobod). No public comparables exist in this subsector, constraining the triangulation approach.

The valuation analysis applied stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable method given data constraints. Using the company's $15M total capital raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $30M. This method directly reflects observed financing-stage transitions but carries heightened model risk due to the narrow comp set and absence of public benchmarks for cross-validation.

The triangulated range spans $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a median point estimate of $30M. The symmetry of this range around the stage-progression result reflects limited independent method corroboration; the single-method foundation substantially narrows conviction in any point within the band. Key uncertainties include unit economics validation, path to Series B fundraising (which would test the 2.0x assumption), and comparability of the two private peers across operational metrics and market positioning. Expansion of the comp set or introduction of revenue multiples would materially improve estimate robustness.
